prerequisites: Solid command of basic arithmetic, differential and integral calculus, as well as physical quantities and SI units, stoichiometry in chemical equations.
Ability to handle Newtonian mechanics, force equilibria, mechanical work within simple examples.

Knowledge of theory and application through examples of equations of state, 1st and 2nd law of thermodynamics, thermodynamic cycles, exergy concept, multi-component systems, thermodynamic processes in technical applications, fundamentals of heat exchange.
Successful completion of the StEOP (preliminary study and orientation phase).

learning_outcomes.text: To concisely present optimal thermodynamic fundamentals for energy technology and internal combustion engines.
To comprehensibly explain important fundamentals of multi-component thermodynamics for energy technology, as well as their application to thermodynamic problems.
To reliably distinguish challenging thermodynamic problems.
To solve challenging thermodynamic problems purposefully.
To independently solve tasks with thermodynamic boundary conditions.
To structuredly explain energy-related, ecological, and energy-economic boundary conditions in a societal context.
To competently describe generalized equations of state for multi-component systems.
To clearly present membrane equilibria in the context of thermodynamics.
To purposefully apply reaction kinetic concepts to problem-related questions.
To name central aspects of energy-related, ecological, and energy-economic boundary conditions for our society.
To independently structure complex problems and present solution approaches.
To compare within the framework of partner and group work as well as peer feedback.
To process complex tasks both independently and in groups.
To clearly formulate roles, responsibilities, and communication rules in a team.
To discuss constructive peer feedback appreciatively.

syllabus_topics: Generalized equations of state for multi-component mixtures
Thermodynamic description of thermal mass separation processes
